claims.text: The driver never answered the rider's locating message, and POL-NS-04 limbs (a) and (b) are made out on this record. At 17:25:36, inside the waiting window, the rider sent a locating message identifying herself and her position ('this is Mei Ling ... im near the Tan Tock Seng Hospital bus stop side'), and at 17:26:06 she sent 'coming down now'. The driver's only message in the log (MSG-03201-001, 17:24:11, 'hi im at the pickup point, where are you') predates both, nothing from him appears in the log after 17:25:36, and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, so he neither replied within 120 seconds of her locating message nor placed an in-app call at any point before terminating the trip at 17:30:38 - 302 seconds of silence on the only channel he had in front of him.

I do not stretch limb (c) of POL-NS-04 to complete that exoneration: it cannot be satisfied on the rider's own track, so POL-NS-04 does not dispose of this dispute. Her device logged 77 fixes between 17:21:00 and 17:32:27 and places her between 599.17 m and 605.94 m from the pickup pin throughout the waiting window, with 0 fixes inside the 100 m rider-presence radius for a STANDARD pickup, so the majority-of-qualifying-fixes test is not met on distance. If those fixes report no accuracy the test is instead unrunnable, and POL-NS-11 makes an unrunnable rider-presence test neutral rather than favourable, requiring the judge to record that the test could not be run rather than inferring the rider was elsewhere. On either reading the rider is not exonerated under POL-NS-04, and the fee falls to be decided under the remaining clauses.

Limb (b) of POL-NS-01 is not affirmatively established on this export, and the gap is one the rider is entitled to have noticed rather than assumed away. POL-NS-02 admits the driver as 'arrived' only where the gps_trace contains at least three consecutive position fixes 'each with reported horizontal accuracy of 25 m or better', and the arrival radius for this STANDARD pickup is 50 m. EV-GPS-03201's summary and the derived arrival block report fix counts, distances and speeds for the driver's 94 fixes, but no accuracy figure for any of them; the derived facts label 42 fixes 'qualifying', and that label tracks distance, so no fix on the record is shown to satisfy the clause's accuracy limb. POL-NS-12 cannot fill that gap: it bridges a sparse or accuracy-less export only where trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is GPS_AUTO, and this record's marker is BUTTON (trip_record.events, 'Driver tapped I'm Here'), which POL-NS-12 states in terms is not covered - so on a BUTTON arrival the export's own fixes must carry the test. The rider does not assert that the driver's fixes were inaccurate; she asserts that the record does not report the accuracy POL-NS-02 requires, so proximity data alone does not establish limb (b). Where the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix, POL-NS-02's own terms apply: the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee with no driver compensation.

claims.text: The GPS trace places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at 17:23:46 — the same second as the trip record's 'arrived' event — and keeps him there across 42 consecutive qualifying fixes in a single unbroken run, comfortably satisfying the three-consecutive-fix proximity test of POL-NS-02 and establishing arrival for POL-NS-01 limb (b).

The in-geofence dwell, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 17:23:46 to the last at 17:30:36, is 410 continuous seconds — 230 seconds more than the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip under trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec — so POL-NS-01 limb (c) holds and the shortfall route of POL-NS-06 is simply unavailable to the rider.

The trip record shows no boarding event and a driver termination at 17:30:38 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, two seconds after the qualifying dwell completed at 17:30:36 — that is a recognised code under POL-NS-01 limb (d), and it falls after the required dwell elapsed, so all four limbs of the anchor clause are made out.

The 'arrived' marker is not a false marker under POL-NS-05: the trace puts the driver stationary inside the arrival radius at the marker's own timestamp of 17:23:46, neither more than 300 m from the pin nor travelling at or above 15 km/h; and in any event limb (iii) applies, because on a clock recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix the dwell is 410 seconds, above the minimum, so the fee stands regardless.

No POL-NS-08 impairment is engaged on the facts that decide this case: the 'arrived' event at 17:23:46 and the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 17:23:46 agree to the second (no limb (a) clock skew), the trace carries 94 fixes at a 10-second cadence with 100.0% coverage and zero gaps inside the waiting window (no limb (b) defect), the chat log's 3 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count with intact msg_id sequence (no limb (c) defect), and the 4.50 fare line reconciles exactly with the platform_policy cancellation fee of 4.50 (no limb (d) defect).

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider, because it requires all three limbs and limb (c) is affirmatively failed on admissible fixes: the rider's own track is present and carries 77 fixes, and they place her device between 599 m and 606 m from the pickup pin, with zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. This is not the undecidable case of POL-NS-11 — the test was run, and it failed.

POL-NS-03 does not rescue the rider either: that clause governs a driver stationary outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin, and the trace puts this driver inside the radius itself, so the wrong-entrance compromise, and the 50 percent pin-ambiguity goodwill that goes with it, never arise.

The chat log shows the driver did the coordinating from the pin, messaging at 17:24:11 'hi im at the pickup point, where are you', and then holding position through the rider's replies of 17:25:36 and 17:26:06 ('coming down now') until 17:30:38 — over four further minutes of waiting after the rider said she was on her way.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-03201-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no payload — no advisory covers this pickup in this window — so the accumulation limb POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable; that costs the driver nothing here, because his dwell is one uninterrupted 410-second run at a single in-geofence position (run_count 1) that already exceeds the minimum without summing any second interval. The absence of an advisory is disclosed, and the impairment is immaterial to this claim.

The rider's account that she was 'only a few minutes late' and that the 4.50 was taken 'for nothing' is not supported by the record: the driver waited 410 seconds from geofence entry before terminating, and the rider's device was still roughly 600 m from the pickup pin at the moment of cancellation, so her narrative of a car that vanished on a punctual rider is contradicted by the trace.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the 4.50 fee in force, SGD 3.60 — the very figure the fare ledger computes under POL-NS-07 — and the anti-farming check does not trip, because driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0 against 95 completed trips in 30 days, below both the absolute-count and the rate limb.

The disposition follows from POL-GEN-03: on this rider-filed dispute the claim is not supported and the 4.50 charge stands in its present state (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), while the outcome value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd mirroring the SGD 3.60 driver_compensation_sgd — the two are not netted.

ruling.explanation: To both parties: this decides the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-03201. What the record shows. The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 17:23:46; the free waiting period in force was 180 s (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec); the wait timer started at 17:23:48; the driver cancelled at 17:30:38 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. The GPS trace records a single unbroken in-geofence run of 410 s (42 fixes), and the rider's own device sits 599-606 m from the pickup pin throughout the window, so the rider was not at the pickup point and the driver's account of a rider who did not appear is consistent with the trace. Why the fee is refunded in full (SGD 4.50). POL-NS-01 charges a no-show fee only if all four of its limbs hold, and limb (b) requires the gps_trace to place the driver inside the pickup geofence on the terms of POL-NS-02. That clause deems the driver arrived only where the trace contains at least three consecutive fixes 'each with reported horizontal accuracy of 25 m or better' within the arrival radius (50 m for this STANDARD pickup). EV-GPS-03201 reports no horizontal accuracy for any of its fixes: its payload carries fix counts, distances and speeds, and its derived block carries no accuracy value at all; the '42 qualifying fixes' and the 410 s run rest on distance and dwell alone. POL-NS-12, which lets platform telemetry stand in for a sparse or accuracy-less export, does not apply: it operates only where platform_policy.arrival_marker is GPS_AUTO and the platform's arrival event states its own geofence test, and this record's marker is BUTTON ('Driver tapped I'm Here'), which POL-NS-12 says in terms is not covered. Limb (b) is therefore not established on this record, the closing sentence of POL-NS-02 follows, and the cancellation fee is refunded in full; no driver compensation is payable. Claims addressed. Driver's claims 1-4 (arrival inside the 50 m radius, the 410 s dwell against the 180 s minimum, termination under RIDER_NO_SHOW after the dwell, and the marker not being false under POL-NS-05) are accepted as far as they go - the marker is genuine and the dwell is real - but proximity, dwell and a genuine marker do not supply the accuracy POL-NS-02 requires, so they do not make limb (b) out. Driver's claim 5 (no POL-NS-08 impairment) is accepted: there is no clock skew, no trace gap, no chat defect and no fare mismatch; a missing accuracy figure is not an impairment under POL-NS-08(a)-(d), so it neither escalates the case nor lifts the clause's own test. Driver's claims 6-7 (POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider, POL-NS-03 does not apply) are accepted and are immaterial, because the fee fails on the driver's own limb (b). Driver's claims 8-9 (the chat log shows the driver coordinating from the pin, and the rider's 'only a few minutes late' account is contradicted by her track 600 m away) are accepted as facts but do not cure limb (b); the driver's counterparty statement is likewise noted but no clause of this category names a counterparty statement as the test for arrival. Driver's claims 10-11 (POL-NS-07 payout of 80% of 4.50 = SGD 3.60, anti-farming clear, and a DRIVER_COMPENSATION disposition) are rejected in their outcome: the arithmetic is right and the anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d 0 against 95 completed trips in 30 days), but compensation only arises where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not. Rider's claims 1-2 (POL-NS-04 limbs (a) and (b) are made out but limb (c) is not) are accepted; POL-NS-04 therefore exonerates no one, and this is immaterial to the outcome. Rider's claim 3 is accepted and decides the case for the reasons above. Discarded claim: the driver's claim about the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-03201-01 was discarded by the referee because it cited a zero-weight artifact (MISSING_ARTIFACT) without naming its issue code, as POL-GEN-02(1) requires; it is not relied on here. The monetary effect, a SGD 4.50 refund, does not exceed the SGD 8.00 execution threshold. Confidence is 0.85: the ruling rests on EV-GPS-03201 and EV-TRIP-03201, each at full weight 1.0, and no relied-on artifact sits below the 0.70 floor.

ruling.explanation:
To Ms Tan (rider) and DRV-10201 (driver): the $4.50 no-show cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full, and no compensation is payable to the driver.

Why the fee does not stand. A no-show fee is chargeable only if all four conditions of POL-NS-01 hold. Limb (b) requires the gps_trace to place the driver inside the pickup geofence as that geofence is defined in POL-NS-02 — and POL-NS-02 requires at least three consecutive fixes, each carrying a reported horizontal accuracy of 25 m or better, within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius. EV-GPS-03201 reports fix counts, distances and speeds for the driver's 94 fixes, but no horizontal accuracy for any of them. The 42 fixes the derived arrival block labels 'qualifying' are in-radius by distance; nothing on the record certifies them to 25 m. By the policy's integrity block a fix with no reported accuracy is 'treated as of unknown accuracy for POL-NS-02 and is neither counted nor excluded by the 25 m filter', so none of those fixes is shown to satisfy the accuracy limb. POL-NS-12 cannot fill the gap: it lets the platform's own arrival and wait-timer events stand in for a sparse or accuracy-less export, but only where trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is GPS_AUTO. Here the marker is BUTTON (the record reads 'Driver tapped I'm Here'), and POL-NS-12 says in terms that a driver-pressed marker is not covered. The export's own fixes must carry the test, and they cannot. Because the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix, POL-NS-02's own terms apply: the driver is not deemed to have arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the $4.50 cancellation fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation.

What this ruling does NOT find. The driver did hold position from 17:23:46 to 17:30:36 — 410 seconds against the 180-second free waiting period — and the trace's closest fix sits 0 m from the pin. Ms Tan's device was 599 m to 606 m from the pin throughout, and she messaged 'coming down now' at 17:26:06. None of that is disputed. The refund rests only on the record's failure to carry the accuracy POL-NS-02 requires before an arrival counts; it is a gap in the driver's proof of arrival, not a finding that he was elsewhere.

The driver's claims, answered. Accepted: the trace shows a single unbroken 410-second in-geofence run (limb (c), over the 180-second minimum, so the POL-NS-06 shortfall route is unavailable to the rider); the trip was terminated by the driver under RIDER_NO_SHOW after the dwell elapsed (limb (d)); the arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05, because at 17:23:46 the trace places the driver inside 50 m of the pin at zero speed, neither beyond 300 m nor at 15 km/h or more; and no POL-NS-08 limb (a) to (d) fires — the arrived event and the first in-geofence fix agree to the second, the trace has 94 fixes over 10-second cadence with 100% coverage and no gaps, the chat log's 3 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count with intact numbering, and the $4.50 fare line reconciles with the platform_policy cancellation fee. But a satisfied limb (c) and a valid limb (d) cannot substitute for a failed limb (b), which POL-NS-01 requires all four to satisfy; and POL-NS-05's distance-and-speed test decides only whether the marker is false, not whether arrival under POL-NS-02 is established. Rejected: the claim that the driver's arrival is established by 42 consecutive fixes (the accuracy limb is unmet), and the claim for SGD 3.60 under POL-NS-07 — compensation requires POL-NS-01 satisfied in full, and it is not. Also accepted: POL-NS-03 does not apply (the driver's stationary fixes are inside the radius, not outside it within 400 m, and the trip has one registered pickup point, so no pin-ambiguity goodwill arises).

The rider's claims, answered. Her POL-NS-04 argument is accepted: limbs (a) and (b) are made out (her locating message at 17:25:36 was not answered within 120 seconds and no in-app call was placed), but limb (c) is not satisfied — her track puts her 599.17 m to 605.94 m from the pin with zero fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius — so POL-NS-04 does not exonerate her, and POL-NS-11 does not change that. Her refund comes from POL-NS-02, not POL-NS-04. Her narrative of 'only a few minutes late' is not borne out, but the fee does not stand for that reason; it stands or falls on the arrival test, which the record does not satisfy.

Discarded evidence. The driver's claim about the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-03201-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) was discarded by the referee for citing an impaired artifact without naming its issue codes; the absence is on the record and immaterial to this outcome. The driver's counterparty statement carries no weight multiplier and does not move the confidence cap.

Execution and appeal. The monetary effect, $4.50, is below the $8.00 automatic-execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so the refund issues on release without a human queue. This is a provisional ruling: either party may appeal once under POL-GEN-04, and the natural cure for the defect here is a record-type addition (a GPS export carrying horizontal accuracy), which an appeal may add. Confidence 0.85, capped by the deciding artifact EV-GPS-03201 at weight_multiplier 1.0.

Both parties: this is about the $4.50 no-show cancellation fee on trip TRP-03201, terminated by the driver at 17:30:38 on 14 Sep under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW.

The platform may treat the driver as having 'arrived' at the pickup pin only if the GPS export contains at least three consecutive in-geofence fixes each carrying a REPORTED horizontal accuracy of 25 m or better (POL-NS-02, read with POL-NS-01 limb (b)). EV-GPS-03201 reports fix counts, distances and speeds for the driver's 94 fixes but no accuracy figure for any of them; the summary's '42 qualifying fixes' is a radius-only count (your own device's qualifying count is 0 on distance alone, as your device sat about 600 m from the pin throughout), so the accuracy limb POL-NS-02 requires is simply not shown on this record. POL-NS-12, which lets the platform's own arrival and wait-timer events stand in for a sparse or accuracy-less export, applies only where trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is GPS_AUTO; this trip's marker is BUTTON (the driver tapped 'I'm Here', trip_record.events), which POL-NS-12 states in terms it does not cover. With no qualifying in-radius fix established, POL-NS-02's own terms apply: POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails and the cancellation fee is refunded in full, with no driver compensation. POL-NS-06's shortfall route is not needed, and POL-NS-03 does not apply because the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the 50 m radius, not outside it.

To the driver: I do not disbelieve your account. The record shows you tapped 'I'm Here' at 17:23:46 and held position at the pin until you cancelled at 17:30:38 — a 410-second dwell, 230 seconds beyond the 180-second free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec) — and the rider's device stayed roughly 600 m away. Your chat message at 17:24:11 and your counterparty statement are consistent with genuine waiting. But the fee is chargeable only if the arrival test is established from the GPS export, and on this export it is not, for the reason given above. Your POL-NS-07 claim to SGD 3.60 (80% of the $4.50 fee, per the fare ledger's POL-NS-07 computation) falls away with it, because it depends on POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full. No referral arises: the arrival marker was not false, so POL-NS-05(ii) is not engaged, and no clause directs an instruction to a human reviewer.

Claims on the same point answered together: (i) the driver's claims that arrival, the 410 s dwell, the RIDER_NO_SHOW code and the absence of a false marker are made out are accepted as arithmetic, but limb (b) fails, so none of them carries the fee; (ii) the driver's claim that no POL-NS-08 impairment is engaged is accepted — the trace has 100% coverage, no gaps, both tracks and a reconciling $4.50 fare line — but that is a different question from POL-NS-02's accuracy requirement; (iii) the driver's claims that POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider and that POL-NS-03 does not rescue her are accepted; (iv) the rider's claims that POL-NS-04 limbs (a) and (b) are made out but limb (c) fails on her own track (599–606 m, 0 qualifying fixes), and that POL-NS-11 makes that neutral rather than favourable, are accepted; (v) the rider's claim that limb (b) is not affirmatively established is accepted and is the ground of decision. The advisory EV-ADVIS-03201-01 (MISSING, weight 0.0) was discarded by the referee for non-disclosure of its issue code and is in any case immaterial, because the driver's dwell is a single unbroken 410 s run needing no accumulation under POL-NS-06(i).

Confidence: 0.85. The deciding fact is carried by EV-GPS-03201 at weight 1.0 (and the BUTTON marker by EV-TRIP-03201 at 1.0); no artifact below 1.0 carries it, so POL-GEN-02(2)'s cap is 1.0. The monetary effect ($4.50) is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of $8.00, so it executes on issue, subject to the POL-GEN-04 appeal route.

ruling.explanation:
To Rider Tan Mei Ling and Driver DRV-10201: the $4.50 no-show fee stands, and the driver is paid $3.60 of it as compensation. The driver did arrive and did wait.

What the record shows. The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 17:23:46, and EV-GPS-03201 independently places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup geofence from that same second, holding position for a single unbroken run of 410 seconds to 17:30:36 — 230 seconds longer than the 180-second free waiting period this trip's platform_policy.free_wait_sec carries. There is no boarding event, and the driver ended the trip at 17:30:38 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, two seconds after the dwell completed. That makes out all four limbs of POL-NS-01, and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it.

Your points, Ms Tan. You said you were only a few minutes late and that the charge was taken for nothing. Your own device track puts you between 599 m and 606 m from the pickup pin throughout the waiting window — roughly six hundred metres away, not a few steps — and after your 'coming down now' message at 17:26:06 the driver waited a further 272 seconds before cancelling. POL-NS-04 cannot excuse the fee: it requires all three limbs, and limb (c) fails because you were never inside the 100 m rider-presence radius on your own admissible fixes (and if your fixes carried no accuracy the answer is the same under POL-NS-11 — an unrunnable presence test cannot exonerate you either way).

Your argument that POL-NS-02 limb (b) is unproven because no fix reports an accuracy figure is rejected. The trace's computed facts were produced by applying this policy's own filters — the derived thresholds name the 25 m accuracy filter and the 50 m STANDARD radius — and they report 42 consecutive qualifying in-geofence fixes, not a distance-only label. POL-NS-12 is correctly not available because the arrival marker is BUTTON, but that does not matter: the exported trace itself carries limb (b).

Driver's points. POL-NS-05 does not fire: you were stationary inside the radius at the marker's own timestamp of 17:23:46, so the marker is not false and no false-arrival referral is made. POL-NS-06 helps neither side: the dwell already exceeds the minimum, and its accumulation limb is unavailable because advisory EV-ADVIS-03201-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — that impairment is immaterial to the deciding facts and is named here as POL-GEN-02(3) requires; the driver claim resting on it was discarded by the referee for non-disclosure. POL-NS-03 does not apply because the driver was inside the arrival radius, not merely within 400 m of the bin. POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the $4.50 fee in force = $3.60; the anti-farming check does not trip (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0, below the absolute-count limb, against 95 completed trips in 30 days).

Confidence. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts — EV-TRIP-03201, EV-GPS-03201, EV-CHAT-03201 and EV-FARE-03201 — has weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and my confidence is 0.9, above the 0.70 floor. The only impaired artifact, the MISSING advisory at 0.0, carries no deciding fact.

Outcome. Under POL-GEN-03 your claim is not supported and the $4.50 charge stands (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). The outcome value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd $3.60 mirroring driver_compensation_sgd $3.60; the fee is not a second payment and is not netted. No clause produces a referral. The monetary effect of $3.60 is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of $8.00, so it executes on issue subject to POL-GEN-04.

ledger.claim: The rider's account that she was 'only a few minutes late' and that the 4.50 was taken 'for nothing' is not supported by the record: the driver waited 410 seconds from geofence entry before terminating, and the rider's device was still roughly 600 m from the pickup pin at the moment of cancellation, so her narrative of a car that vanished on a punctual rider is contradicted by the trace.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the 4.50 fee in force, SGD 3.60 — the very figure the fare ledger computes under POL-NS-07 — and the anti-farming check does not trip, because driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0 against 95 completed trips in 30 days, below both the absolute-count and the rate limb.

The disposition follows from POL-GEN-03: on this rider-filed dispute the claim is not supported and the 4.50 charge stands in its present state (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), while the outcome value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd mirroring the SGD 3.60 driver_compensation_sgd — the two are not netted.
